strengths: Strong empirical results with impressive speedups (15.63× on LLaDA, 34.22× with caching) while maintaining competitive accuracy
Clear problem motivation and well-articulated discussion of why existing static sampling strategies are suboptimal
Broad experimental coverage across 8 benchmarks and 2 different diffusion LLM architectures
Detailed ablation studies on key hyperparameters with clear sensitivity analysis
Good algorithmic presentation with clear mathematical formulations and visual illustrations of the two-stage pipeline
Demonstrates practical value by outperforming autoregressive LLaMA3 8B in throughput while maintaining comparable accuracy
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty—the core contribution is an adaptive token selection heuristic without deep theoretical insights or justification
The 'three golden principles' are straightforward observations rather than fundamental insights; they represent obvious properties of iterative refinement rather than novel discoveries
Reproducibility concerns: marked code as 'Code:' with no actual repository link, no confidence intervals, no multiple runs reported, hyperparameter selection methodology unclear
Non-negligible accuracy degradation on several benchmarks (Math: -0.52, MMLU-pro: -1.23, BBH: -1.28), contradicting 'minimal drop' claims; no analysis of failure cases

strengths: Clear articulation of three empirically-grounded principles (Certainty, Convergence, Positional) that effectively guide the sampling strategy design, supported by good visualization and intuition

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 benchmarks and 2 dLLM architectures with strong results: up to 15.63× speedup alone and 34.22× with caching, demonstrating dLLMs can match/exceed autoregressive LLM throughput
Thorough ablation studies examining key hyperparameters (τmin_conf, τhigh_conf, Kmax, Whist, σ²stable) with clear sensitivity analysis and well-motivated default values
Well-designed two-stage pipeline that is technically sound with clear mathematical formulations and good engineering integration with existing dLLM-Cache mechanisms
Maintains comparable accuracy while achieving substantial speedups in most cases (minimal degradation <1% on many benchmarks), providing good speed-quality trade-offs
weaknesses: Core novelty is limited—the three principles are relatively straightforward empirical observations, and the technical contribution primarily applies these to engineer a practical system rather than introducing novel methodological insights

Method introduces 7+ hyperparameters requiring tuning (τmin_conf, τhigh_conf, Kmax, Whist, σ²stable, kslow, kfast); lacks principled guidance for hyperparameter selection on new models/tasks without validation data

Some accuracy-speed trade-offs are non-trivial (e.g., GPQA: -2.68% at 34.22× speedup); paper underexplores analysis of accuracy degradation patterns and does not provide guidance for choosing hyperparameters based on desired accuracy targets

Several technical design choices lack strong justification: Why is variance of convergence horizon the right stability metric? Why is the simple max operation optimal for End Point prediction (Eq. 7)? 'Aggressive unmasking' vaguely specified
Experimental evaluation limited to single GPU (RTX 4090); no multi-GPU scaling, statistical significance testing, or error bars; some baseline comparisons (semi-autoregressive) appear underdeveloped

Incomplete analysis of failure modes and edge cases; no discussion of sequence length sensitivity, very short sequences, or guidance on when NOT to use the method; how does exploratory stage length vary by task?

Figure 3 is dense and difficult to parse; notation inconsistencies across indices; title 'Three Golden Principles' feels somewhat marketing-oriented; limited discussion of related speculative decoding and parallel inference methods

Stability check design appears ad-hoc and empirically optimized without theoretical justification; Whist=2 seems very small and no analysis provided of how often stability criterion is met or typical exploratory stage lengths

strengths: Substantial and impressive speedups (15-34×) with practical significance; LLaDA with SlowFast+Cache outperforms LLaMA3 8B in throughput while maintaining competitive accuracy
Comprehensive evaluation across 8 diverse benchmarks and 2 dLLM models with multiple baselines and thorough ablation studies
Excellent reproducibility with detailed algorithm specification, hyperparameter configurations, case studies, and promised code release
Demonstrates clean composability with existing acceleration methods (dLLM-Cache), showing orthogonal improvements
Well-executed experimental work with clear presentation and effective visualizations of the confidence dynamics
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: confidence-based sampling, convergence detection, and positional clustering are known techniques; the core contribution is their algorithmic combination rather than fundamental innovation

Overclaiming about accuracy: Tables 1-2 show notable accuracy drops on several tasks (Dream -1.23% to -3.20%, LLaDA up to -0.52%), contradicting claims of 'lossless acceleration' and 'minimal accuracy drop'

High hyperparameter complexity with 7 key parameters requiring tuning; methodology for hyperparameter selection (τmin_conf=0.1, τhigh_conf=0.85) not clearly explained; transferability to new models unclear
Limited generalization: only 2 dLLM models tested (both 2025 models); no evidence the method generalizes to other dLLM architectures; unclear if results persist as the emerging dLLM field matures

Weak theoretical foundation: stability check using variance is ad-hoc with no justification for this choice; no theoretical analysis of why principles should work; connection between confidence convergence and correct decoding assumed rather than proven

Positional Principle underspecified and least well-motivated; could result from other factors (prompt bias, local context); non-contiguous block handling seems to require additional mechanisms not fully explained

Incomplete analysis: no investigation of failure modes; unexplained variance in benchmark speedups (GSM8K 3.2× vs BBH 5.24×); Figure 1(b) confidence map intriguing but underanalyzed; missing memory/latency analysis
Missing comparisons: limited baselines beyond Fast-dLLM; no statistical significance testing; no comparison with other acceleration approaches (distillation, quantization, speculative decoding)

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 benchmarks with consistent speedup results (15.63× to 34.22×)
Well-motivated problem identification: existing static sampling strategies are inflexible and suboptimal
Strong empirical results with generally maintained accuracy, demonstrating practical utility
Detailed ablation studies and hyperparameter sensitivity analysis (Figures 5-8) showing robustness
Good integration with existing caching mechanisms (dLLM-Cache) enabling even larger speedups
Clear algorithmic description with formal definitions and algorithm pseudocode
Practical demonstration of outperforming autoregressive models in throughput
weaknesses: Limited novelty: confidence-based token selection and convergence monitoring are existing techniques; the main contribution is combining these in a two-stage framework, which is incremental engineering rather than conceptual innovation
Misleading framing of heuristic observations as 'golden principles'—these are empirical observations without theoretical justification or deep insight
Shallow analysis of core mechanisms: insufficient explanation of why high-confidence tokens remain stable, under what conditions convergence occurs, or why spatial clustering emerges
Arbitrary design choices: variance as stability metric (Eq. 8-9), mean for aggregation (Eq. 9), and threshold values (τ_min_conf=0.1, τ_high_conf=0.85) lack principled justification
Significant accuracy drops contradict claims of 'minimal accuracy loss': GPQA drops 2.68%, MMLU-pro (Dream) drops 2.33%, Math (Dream) drops 1.58%
Fragile algorithmic decisions: Eq. 7 end-point definition could jump ahead if confidence spikes at distant positions; fallback refinement threshold (< 1 token) is ad-hoc
Five hyperparameters plus k_slow/k_fast require tuning; unclear if settings generalize to new tasks and models beyond LLaDA/Dream
Limited baseline comparisons: missing evaluations against Sparse-dLLM, dKV-Cache, and other concurrent acceleration methods mentioned in related work
Reproducibility gaps: variance computation specifics, tie-breaking in top-k, caching-forward pass interaction, and computational overhead of stability checking not detailed

Questionable autoregressive comparison: Table 4 claims outperformance but compares 28.79% accuracy (LLaDA+SlowFast+Cache) vs 31.92% (LLaMA3)—this is throughput-accuracy tradeoff, not genuine superiority
Limited evaluation scope: single GPU only, only 2 dLLM models tested, unclear effects of varying sequence lengths (3-256 tokens across benchmarks)
Positional principle is least analyzed; spatial clustering is observed but not deeply explained, and its contribution to acceleration is unclear
Algorithm 1 ambiguities: conditions for triggering fallback refinement are reactive rather than proactive; k_slow selection logic not fully specified

strengths: Strong empirical results with impressive speedups (15.63-34.22×) and minimal accuracy drops, outperforming LLaMA3 8B in throughput
Well-motivated three golden principles with clear intuitive explanations and effective visualizations of the key insights
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 8 benchmarks and 2 dLLM models with thorough hyperparameter sensitivity analysis
Practical compatibility with existing acceleration techniques (dLLM-Cache) demonstrating orthogonal benefits
Solid technical execution with detailed algorithm description, clear presentation, and good reproducibility practices
Effective case studies and ablation studies demonstrating robustness across diverse tasks
weaknesses: Limited theoretical novelty - the three principles are empirical observations without formal justification or convergence analysis
Positional principle lacks depth: no analysis of why tokens cluster contiguously, when this assumption breaks down, or failure modes
Variance-based stability criterion appears ad-hoc without justification for why variance is the right metric or comparison with alternatives
Multiple hyperparameters (Kmax, Whist, σ²_stable, τmin_conf, τhigh_conf, kslow, kfast) raise generalization concerns despite robustness claims
Incomplete baseline comparisons - semi-autoregressive baseline significantly underperforms without clear explanation; limited comparison with other recent acceleration methods
Unclear contribution attribution between core SlowFast sampling and orthogonal caching mechanism, making it harder to isolate the sampling strategy's contribution
Missing analysis of exploratory stage computational overhead and scalability to very long sequences (>4096 tokens)
Limited failure case analysis - no discussion of tasks/prompts where positional clustering breaks down or robustness to distribution shift
Aggregation choice for convergence horizon (mean vs median) in Eq. 9 appears arbitrary without sensitivity analysis
